narrative.overview:
The page is a quiet sheet of warm paper, and the people on it are the color. Neutrals are brown-tinted grays, never pure black or white, so the surface reads as a calm working canvas. Against it, six saturated peer hues (orange, yellow, green, blue, red, purple) stand for the collaborators themselves: cursors, profile stacks, selections, live edits. Color means "someone is here", which is exactly what the product makes possible.

Orange is the one hue that also belongs to the brand. It carries the logo, the primary call to action, and emphasis in headlines. The other five hues appear together, as a group of peers, not as individual decoration.

The system is flat and precise: hairline borders instead of shadows, small 4px corners on controls, generous vertical spacing between sections. It supports light and dark themes by inverting the gray scale. The site must not read as a generic SaaS template; its identity comes from showing real collaboration on the canvas, not from stock hero patterns.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, brown-tinted neutral scale in both themes
One brand accent (orange); five further peer hues reserved for presence
Pretendard for everything, Roboto Mono for code
Live examples and code are the primary imagery

rules.name: The Peers Rule
rules.body: The five non-orange hues mean "a collaborator". Do not use a single one of them as a decorative accent or a status color on marketing surfaces.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: No pure #000 or cool grays. Every neutral comes from the --gray-* scale. The only literal white is text on a saturated fill.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Do not add a second display typeface. Emphasis in a headline is made with weight or the orange accent.

rules.name: The Flat Canvas Rule
rules.body: Cards and sections at rest have a border and no shadow. Shadows belong to layers that float above the page.

dos: Do use var(--gray-*) and var(--{hue}-*) custom properties so light and dark themes both work.
Do keep orange for brand and primary actions, and show the other hues together as peers.
Do let live examples, cursors, and real code carry the page.
Do separate surfaces with 1px borders and spacing from the 8px scale.
donts: Don't make the site look like a generic SaaS template: no stock purple-blue gradient heroes, no repeated three-card feature rows as the default section pattern, no interchangeable hero with a screenshot under a centered headline.
Don't add shadows to cards at rest.
Don't introduce a second display typeface or cool gray neutrals.
Don't run npm run fetch:ui; it overwrites styles/ from a legacy source.
